r.정치 구도: Voters elect the president directly, and the president appoints a prime minister from the parliamentary majority to form a government. After independence from Belgium in 1960 the country went through long dictatorship and two major wars, and only in 2019 did power change hands peacefully through an election for the first time. It is divided into 26 provinces, but the capital Kinshasa lies more than 1,500 km from the mining regions of the east, so the central government's reach there is weak. In November 2026 the president signed a law allowing a new constitution to be put to a referendum, fuelling fears that the two-term limit on the presidency will be scrapped. With a former president siding with the rebels and the main opposition parties rejecting an offer of dialogue, whether the elections due in late 2028 will happen on time is itself in question.

t.why: It produces most of the world's cobalt, used in EV batteries, and is among the top copper producers. When it banned cobalt exports in 2025 and then switched to quotas, world cobalt prices swung sharply. Chinese companies run a large share of the mines, and in December 2025 the United States signed a strategic partnership with Kinshasa and is backing a rail route to carry minerals to Angola's port of Lobito. In the east, the Rwanda-backed M23 rebels seized Goma and Bukavu in early 2025; separate peace tracks continue with Rwanda under US mediation and with M23 under Qatari mediation, but the fighting has not fully stopped. The Congo Basin, the largest rainforest after the Amazon, also makes it central to the climate debate.
t.rel: It has fought the M23 rebels in the east, said to be backed by Rwanda, and signed a US-brokered peace deal with Rwanda in 2025. Its wealth of minerals such as cobalt draws the attention of the great powers.
t.korea: Diplomatic relations were established in 1963. A national museum built with KOICA support opened in Kinshasa in 2019, and a water treatment plant financed by a Korean government loan was completed in 2023. KOICA has also worked with the UN to clear landmines and explosives in the conflict-hit east, opening the way home for displaced people. To secure steady supplies of cobalt, copper and other critical minerals, the two countries discussed mining and investment cooperation at a joint commission in 2025, and talks on an investment protection agreement are continuing.
t.know: The DRC produces more of the cobalt used in smartphones and electric-vehicle batteries than any other country.
etext: It is the world's largest cobalt producer and among the top copper producers. It also holds lithium, tin, tantalum and gold, making it a storehouse of minerals that batteries and electronics depend on.

The Congo River flows so powerfully that plans to build giant hydropower dams at Inga, enough to light up much of Africa, have circulated for decades. Its vast rainforest draws attention as a carbon sink.

Minerals leave the country with little processing, so most of the added value goes abroad. Poor roads and power leave the mining regions all but cut off from the capital, and conflict in the east, corruption and child labor in small hand-dug mines hold back investment.
